target: ERIN jury validation: "80 cases adjudicated by Claude" and jury-smoke claims of five models at "100% vs adjudicated truth"
flaw: The purported ground truth is generated by Claude, while the candidate labelers are LLMs applying a closely related prompt to the same reports. This is a self-validation loop, not independent clinical validation; the planned Rehan spot-check of 10 cases was still pending, and cancer-only agreement on 79 selected difficult cases cannot establish multiclass grade accuracy across 7,149 reports.
fix: Obtain blinded adjudication by at least two gastrointestinal pathologists for a stratified random sample, enriched for disagreements but including routine cases, with consensus resolution and per-class accuracy, weighted kappa, sensitivity, and specificity reported against that independent reference.

target: ERIN Ch3 primary endpoint: "current-biopsy grade classification" using "report-derived grade"; clinical arm includes "report-derived structured variables"
flaw: The target is extracted from the pathology report, while the second modality is also derived from pathology-report information. Even if the intended variables are prior-timepoint only, no completed temporal provenance audit demonstrates that same-report grade wording, contemporaneous cancer-pathway information, or post-biopsy documentation cannot enter the clinical arm; this can manufacture a fusion benefit without adding predictive information.
fix: Produce a patient-timepoint data dictionary and automated audit proving every clinical feature predates the indexed biopsy and target report. Repeat the primary analysis with independently curated slide-grade labels, or restrict the clinical arm to prospectively available non-report variables such as age, sex, prior surveillance history, and pre-index records.

target: OCCAMS v3: "shuffled controls omitted" despite the frozen protocol stating "Every prediction task is accompanied by a shuffled-label control"
flaw: The plan explicitly treats a non-chance shuffled-label result as pipeline-invalidating, yet the decisive OCCAMS v3 survival run omitted this control. With only n=87 and 58 events, this is not a cosmetic deviation: the central negative fusion conclusion lacks the prespecified test that the survival pipeline is behaving correctly.
fix: Run shuffled-outcome controls through the identical fold construction, Cox fitting, seed averaging, and bootstrap procedure before interpreting v3. Mark the current result exploratory until the control, code hash, and out-of-fold row contract have been independently checked.

target: SWGCohort claim: "Late-mean fusion is the best family" and the thesis-hypothesis contrast "fusion minus histology-only" of +0.073 AUPRC/+0.043 AUC, where the paired bootstrap CI is "[pending]"
flaw: The stated thesis question is whether fusion beats histology, but the only reported inferential result is fusion versus copy number (+0.111 AUC, CI 0.002 to 0.219). The AUPRC fusion-versus-copy-number CI crosses zero, and there is no CI at all for the primary fusion-versus-histology contrast, so the claimed "likely multimodal benefit" is not supported by the specified comparison.
fix: Compute and report patient-level paired bootstrap CIs for fusion minus histology for AUPRC, AUC, Brier score, and predeclared net-benefit thresholds from locked OOF predictions. Do not make a fusion-benefit claim unless the prespecified fusion-versus-histology interval excludes zero.

target: Adoption of jury labels: original ERIN consensus had "3,350 confident / 2,860 uncertain", whereas the jury reports "6,867 train_eligible" and only "204 unsure_held_out"
flaw: Eight models trained on overlapping internet and instruction data agreeing with one another is not evidence that 97% of reports are clinically unambiguous. The dramatic collapse from 2,860 uncertain reports to 204 held out risks converting systematic shared LLM errors into apparently high-confidence training labels and preferentially removing difficult cases from evaluation.
fix: Quantify overlap between the original disagreement set and jury-majority labels, validate confidence strata against independent human grades, and retain an uncertainty-stratified test set rather than excluding ambiguous cases wholesale. Report performance separately for unanimous, majority-only, prior-disagreement, and human-adjudicated labels.

target: OCCAMS v3 cohort size: pre-registration specifies "n≈141 patients with both modalities", but v3 reports "n: 87, events: 58" and the plan says this "needs explanation"
flaw: Losing roughly 38% of the intended multimodal cohort without an accounting of exclusions, missingness by modality, event status, and treatment/stage distribution can change both the estimand and the apparent absence of genomics signal. The unexplained n=87 also prevents assessment of whether selection on complete-case availability induced collider bias.
fix: Provide a CONSORT-style attrition table from the full OCCAMS source population to the 87 analysed patients, stratified by survival/event status and every modality. Compare included versus excluded patients, prespecify or justify missing-data handling, and repeat with appropriate imputation or inverse-probability weighting where defensible.

target: Survival uncertainty claims in OCCAMS v3 (n=87, 58 events) and TCGA-OAC (n=65, 36 events): bootstrap CIs from one frozen 5-fold CV design
flaw: Bootstrapping fixed OOF predictions quantifies sampling variation conditional on the selected folds and trained models, but omits split, model-fitting, hyperparameter, and seed-selection uncertainty. At these event counts, declaring histology "signal" from CIs such as OCCAMS C=0.6272, CI 0.5394–0.7109 is therefore more certain than the design warrants.
fix: Use repeated nested patient-level cross-validation or bootstrap refitting, preserving all within-patient records, and report the distribution over resampling, splits, and seeds. Treat the present CIs as conditional descriptive intervals rather than confirmatory evidence.

target: TCGA pooled result: "POOLED OAC+GEJ fusion" / tcga_pool_fusion.json, n=399, with late histology+clinical delta CI [0.0273, 0.0953]
flaw: The expanded pool combines OAC with STAD/GEJ-derived cases after the OAC-only protocol, while R.2 says "primary claim stays OAC-only." A clinical-fusion gain in a mixed anatomical, treatment, and site cohort may be driven by subtype or centre membership, and cannot be represented as a powered replication of the OAC fusion question.
fix: Analyse OAC, GEJ, and gastric/STAD strata separately; include cohort/site and histological subtype as explicit covariates; test interaction terms; and perform leave-cohort-out validation. Label the pooled analysis exploratory unless its pooling and estimand were formally amended before outcome inspection.

target: Amendment-log conclusion: "TP53 AUC 0.678 and WGD 0.703 from H&E" means "genomics IS partially visible at adequate n"
flaw: These post hoc necessity probes are reported without confidence intervals, external validation, stratification by OAC versus GEJ/STAD, or adjustment for multiple genomic and clinical targets. Since tumour subtype, grade, site, tumour purity, and slide acquisition can correlate with TP53/WGD, the result does not establish that molecular alterations themselves are morphologically visible.
fix: Predefine the tested targets, provide patient-bootstrap CIs and multiplicity correction, and test within homogeneous disease/site strata and across held-out cohorts. Add models controlling for stage, subtype, tumour content, and acquisition site before making a biological visibility claim.

target: Chapter 2 comparator plan: "PORPOISE baseline on OCCAMS + TCGA-OAC" remains incomplete, while related_work calls PORPOISE the direct published WSI+molecular fusion comparison
flaw: The thesis proposes conclusions about the adequacy or failure of bespoke late fusion without having run the explicitly planned established multimodal benchmark. Negative results from a custom ABMIL/linear-Cox implementation cannot distinguish absence of multimodal signal from an underperforming architecture or implementation.
fix: Complete PORPOISE under identical patient splits, endpoint definitions, modality availability, and preprocessing as far as feasible; report its OOF fusion-versus-unimodal deltas beside the thesis models. If it cannot be made comparable, narrow the claim to the tested implementation rather than multimodal fusion generally.

target: SWGCohort model selection: seven families plus co-attention are compared, then "Late-mean fusion is the best family"
flaw: Selecting the numerically best of multiple fusion families and then quoting an ordinary paired CI for that selected winner ignores winner's-curse and multiplicity. No supplied SWG pre-registration identifies late-mean as the sole confirmatory model or specifies correction across early, intermediate, late-mean, stacked, and co-attention alternatives.
fix: Either designate the late-mean model as confirmatory before re-analysis, or use nested model selection and evaluate the selected pipeline in outer folds. Report all families with simultaneous/multiplicity-aware uncertainty and describe the current best-family result as exploratory.

target: Encoder-sweep pre-registration: fixed grid of UNI2-h, Virchow2, GigaPath and conditional H-Optimus-0, followed by amendments adding Phikon-v2 and H-Optimus-1 and declaring the grid "FINAL at 6"
flaw: The pre-registration says "No further additions mid-sweep" and prohibits adding encoders because results disappoint, yet the grid was expanded twice after the original freeze. Calling these additions sanctioned by an "own pre-reg clause" is inaccurate: the supplied pre-registration contains no clause permitting Phikon-v2 or H-Optimus-1.
fix: Record the expanded grid as a post-registration amendment with dates, rationale, and whether any results were visible at each decision. Keep the original encoder set as the confirmatory sensitivity analysis and present added encoders as exploratory, with all results reported regardless of direction.
